title: Cheeseburger Smash Tacos
description: Big Mac-style smash tacos: lean mince pressed onto a mini wrap and fried until crisp, finished with cheese, lettuce and burger sauce.

yield.note: About 2 serves. The original post is for 1 taco.

source.name: Social media post (creator not recorded)
source.note: Original post gives amounts for 1 taco and no cooking times.

confidence.note: Ingredients and method from the original post. Scaling to 4 tacos, the pan timers, oil spray, seasoning, lettuce quantity, homemade sauce and variations were added by Claude and are untested.

items.note: Bought, or see the homemade sauce in notes

steps.title: Press the mince
steps.text: Divide the mince ({{mince}}) into 4 equal portions of about {{mince*0.25}}. Press each portion thinly and evenly onto a mini wrap, right to the edges, aiming for about 3mm thick. Season the meat side with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Fry mince-side down
steps.text: Heat a large frying pan or cast iron pan over medium-high heat with a light coat of oil spray, as lean mince can catch without it. Fry the tacos mince-side down, without moving them, until the meat is browned, crispy at the edges and cooked through with no pink showing. Most pans fit 2 at a time.

steps.title: Flip and melt cheese
steps.text: Flip each taco, lay a cheese slice on the meat and cook until the cheese melts and the wrap is lightly toasted.

steps.title: Fill and fold
steps.text: Remove from the pan. Add the shredded lettuce and burger sauce ({{sauce*0.25}} each), then fold or roll into a taco. Eat straight away while the wrap is crisp.

notes.title: Homemade burger sauce
notes.text: Makes enough for about 8 tacos. Mix 4 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tbsp finely chopped gherkin or sweet relish, 1 tsp yellow mustard, 1 tsp white vinegar, and 1/4 tsp each of smoked paprika, onion powder and garlic powder. Rest 10 minutes before using. Untested estimate, not from the original post.

notes.title: Closer to a Big Mac
notes.text: Scatter finely diced white onion and sliced pickles over the lettuce, and press a few sesame seeds into the raw mince before frying.

notes.title: Variations (untested)
items: Mexican beef: mix about two-thirds of a batch of Homemade Taco Seasoning into the mince before pressing. Top with cheddar, lettuce, tomato, sour cream and hot sauce instead of burger sauce.
Korean beef: mix 1 tbsp gochujang, 2 tsp soy sauce and 1 tsp minced garlic into the mince. Top with Japanese Sesame Cabbage Salad and Kewpie mixed with sriracha.

Middle Eastern lamb: use lamb mince with 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander and 1 minced garlic clove. Finish with tomato, cucumber, parsley and tahini dressing or garlic yoghurt. Skip the oil spray.
Chicken: press chicken mince slightly thinner and cook a little longer so it is cooked right through. Finish Caesar-style with cos lettuce, parmesan and Caesar dressing.
Air fryer: mince-side up at 200°C for about 6 to 8 minutes, cheese on for the final minute. Less crust on the meat, and light wraps can lift in the fan, so treat this as a trial.
